newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Gov't steps urged to boost Seoul stock market.
newsitem.headline: Gov't steps urged to boost Seoul stock market.

text.p: The ruling New Korea Party and the Korea Investment Trust Companies' Association on Tuesday urged the government to take steps to boost the sagging stock market, including a delay in the planned sale of Korea Telecom shares.
"The New Korea Party urges the government to draw up and implement measures that can effectively stabilise the stock market," a statement from the party said.

Separately, the investment firms' association said sales of government stakes in Korea Telecom and other state-run companies should be postponed until the composite stock index recovers to over 1,000, compared with with the current 699 level.
The government has said it would sell about 260 billion won worth of Korea Telecom shares to corporations and institutions in an auction on December 12-13.
The investment firms' association also recommended that any new share supply should be limited to below one percent of the gross domestic product, compared with an estimated 2.7 percent this year.
It also asked the government to expand the ceiling of foreign share ownership at the earliest possible date in 1997.
The government has pledged it would increase the ceiling to an aggregate 23 percent during calendar 1997 from the current 20 percent, but no time frame has yet been set.
The association also demanded foreign investment in local non-guaranteed corporate bonds be allowed in 1997, instead of 1998 as originally scheduled.
Officials at the ruling party and the association said their requests had been submitted to the Finance Ministry.
Ministry officials declined to comment on the requests, but said the ministry would carefully review them.
